Verification done against the code, the real artefact, the published tree and the rendered tree. Below: what checked out, then the ranked findings. ## Fix-by-fix verification (all 14 + D54) Everything on the converged list is present in the code, and the real-run artefacts confirm the ones that can be measured: - **(1) root inference** — `invert_theories` (site_source_pages.py:383-438) uses `/thys/` for AFP and `os.path.commonprefix` for the distribution, with the every-path-starts-with-exactly-one-prefix assertion. Real run: 11,524 inverted paths, prefixes `{'$AFP/': './contrib/afp-2026-05-13/thys/', '~~/': './contrib/Isabelle2025-2/'}`. The Naproche shape (`contrib/naproche-1/…`) is in the test fixture. `--repo-root` exists; never exercised by a test. - **(2) merge tolerance / base / caller-rewrites-in-base-dir** — implemented (`merge_aux_copies`:840-886, `run_publish`:1009-1019). Real: 12 conflicts, exactly the 12 the plan names; `_aux/ISABELLE_HOME/src/Provers/splitter.ML.html` line 490 carries `id="HOL.split|attribute"`; `smt_word.ML`/`word_lib.ML`/`util.ML` bases are the copies whose title names the symbolic path. But see findings 1 and 2. - **(3)** gate reads a target only for non-empty fragments; `UnicodeDecodeError` → fail/report. Tested. - **(4)** export checkpoint pins `links_digest`. Tested. - **(5)** CSS externals counted once; gate fails on report-vs-own mismatch. Real: report 232 = gate 232. Tested with a 4-copy fixture. - **(6) identity chain** — verified end to end on the real artefacts: `theories_sha256` = `1d6a34647077f55a…` and `sha256sum data/theories.json` gives the identical digest; `registry_fingerprint` = `{entries: 10666, names_sha256: b444fd4c…}`; `classification.inventory` holds 12,209 entries = 10,595 published + 2 underived + 1,165 aux copies + 335 css + 13 fonts + 99 dropped; the artefact re-hashes to `31a4b060cfb1e563…` and `publish-report.json`'s `artefact_hash` is exactly that string. Gate refuses a mismatched pair (tested). - **(7)** strip reads the sealed inventory, no filesystem probe. Tested. - **(8)** export refuses a missing artefact and the flag pair before any network action — code is right (site_export.py:768-795, moved above `emit_asset`); **no test exists**. - **(9)** gate asserts every classification-promised page. Real tree: 11,750 files = 10,595 + 1,139 + 13 + index + css + report. Tested. - **(10)** unresolvable declaring hashes → `no_evidence`. Real run: 0. Tested. - **(11)** `build_relocation` per-class arity + pre-claimed generated paths — code is right; **no test exists**. - **(12)** dangling scan is href-only. Tested. - **(13)** D51 counter counts anchors ×n. Tested; real run 1. - **(14)** `classify_reference`/`line_fragment`/`line_mark` shared. Yes. - **D54** implemented as two buckets. See findings 3-6. Other real-run confirmations: coverage 99.2821 % positioned and linked (1,327,410 / 1,337,009); 486,346 marks; 9,784/9,784 `.thy` position files resolve, 0 fallback, the bare→`X.X` twin preference fires exactly once (`$AFP/Restriction_Spaces-Examples/HOLCF/Restriction_Spaces-HOLCF.thy`); all three acceptance URLs land (`HOL.HOL.html#L513` on `lemma conjI`, `Forcing.Arities.html#L235` on a `lemma`, `function_pointer.ML.html#L298`); none of the 12 merged pages carries a duplicate id; 109 tests pass. --- ## Findings, ranked **1. HIGH — the merge's title/h1 exemption is per-line and swallows real text differences.** `site_source_pages.py:877-881`. The tolerance skips the text comparison whenever *either* side's line matches `<(title|h1)\b`, so any other difference on that line is forgiven too. Verified by probe: two copies whose `
` content is `REAL CONTENT A` vs `TOTALLY DIFFERENT B` merge silently when the title sits on the same line — "any other difference stops the pass" does not hold. Today safe only because the renderer puts `` on line 6 and `<h1>` on line 12 of a fixed preamble (measured: on all 12 real conflicts exactly lines 6 and 12 invoke the exemption). The amended ruling says "line-for-line in text once the title and heading are set aside" — set aside the *elements' text*, not the *lines*. **Fix:** normalise rather than exempt — `re.sub(r'(<(title|h1)\b[^>]*>)[^<]*', r'\1', line)` on both sides, then compare `_TAG.sub("", …)`. Note the test that should catch this (`test_site_source_pages.py:538`) is built on single-line fixtures where title and source window share a line, so it cannot distinguish the two readings; rewrite it multi-line with a differing body line.

**2. MEDIUM-HIGH — the base rule systematically prefers the foreign render, and two published pages now carry wrong cross-references.**
`merge_aux_copies:858-862`. The renderer emits the symbolic title (`File ‹~~/src/…›`) exactly when the presenting session does *not* own the file, and a session-relative title (`File ‹Tools/smt_word.ML›`) when it does — so "the copy whose title names the symbolic path" is anti-correlated with ownership. Measured consequence on the real tree: for `~~/src/HOL/Library/Tools/smt_word.ML` and `…/word_lib.ML` the base is `Unsorted/AFP-ALL-3/…`, and the published pages link `word`, `ucast`, `scast`, `word_cat`, … to `/source/Zip_Benchmarks.Word.html` — the AFP *Zippy* benchmark's "adjusted copy of HOL-Library.Word" (its own header says so, `contrib/afp-2026-05-13/thys/Zippy/Zippy/Instances/Zip/Examples/Benchmarks/Word.thy`) — while the HOL-Library copy links `HOL-Library.Word`. Nothing dangles (D49's amendment is right that both targets exist), but a reader on the distribution's ML page is sent to a different theory. **Fix direction:** among copies whose title names the symbolic path, prefer one whose rendered session directory is not an umbrella build name; or make ownership the primary key and, since title/h1 lines are exempt anyway, write the symbolic path into the merged title.

**3. MEDIUM — D54's alarm counts distinct (page, fragment) pairs; D51's counts anchors. The gap is 4×.**
`run_gate:1180` (`wanted.setdefault(target_rel, set()).add(fragment)`) discards multiplicity. Measured on the published tree: 694,773 distinct `offset_` (target, fragment) pairs, of which **106 miss** — exactly the reported baseline — but those 106 are pointed at by **425 reference occurrences**, one of them (`HOL.HOL.html#offset_20940..20947`) by 253 references alone. D54's own wording calls them "106 … fragment references". Failure scenario: a future render adds one dead anchor referenced 5,000 times; the standing number goes 106 → 107 and the alarm the "read three numbers" discipline rests on stays flat. **Fix:** make `wanted` a `Counter`, report occurrences alongside pairs, and correct the baseline in §17.5/D54.

**4. MEDIUM — D54's provenance split is "where the gate found it", not evidence of what the input lacked, so every entity-anchor check is now report-only.**
`run_gate:1147-1244`. `wanted` is filled by walking the *published* tree, so anything not composed by us lands in the forgiving bucket — including every entity cross-reference the rewrite passed through. A bug in our own rewriting of inherited fragments would therefore gate green. The existing test proves the shape: `test_an_inherited_fragment_miss_is_reported_not_failed` renames `id="A.B.foo|fact"` in the *published* tree — pure broken-by-us corruption — and asserts `run_gate(...) == 0`. Scope: at least the 694,773 `offset_` pairs plus every entity anchor, including the 266,134 references into auxiliary pages that D49 ruling 6 exists to protect; "the gate stops trusting any fragment and checks them all" has become "checks them all and forgives them all". **Fix direction** in proposal P1 below.

**5. MEDIUM-LOW — a fragment in both buckets fails *and* inflates the D54 alarm with a false message.**
`run_gate:1225-1244`. Verified by probe on the e2e fixture (a page referencing `/source/A.A.html#L1` where `L1` is one of our marks, with the mark removed): output is `FAILURES: 1` *and* `reported, not failed (D54): 1 inherited fragment(s) the rendered tree never anchored` — which is false, the fragment is ours. Latent today (`grep -P 'href="[^"]*#L\d+"'` over the published tree returns 0). **Fix:** `inherited = {f for f in wanted.get(rel, ()) if f} - own`.

**6. MEDIUM-LOW — our own generated pages are classified "inherited".**
Same walk as #4: `/source/index.html` and `/source/isabelle.css` are ours, yet fragments found in them go to the forgiving bucket. Harmless today (neither emits a fragment); the obvious next feature — per-session jump anchors in the index — puts a generator bug into the tolerated class.

**7. MEDIUM-LOW — converged fixes with no test.**
(a) `build_relocation`'s per-class collision arity and the pre-claimed `GENERATED_PAGES` (fix 11): grep for `build_relocation`/`GENERATED_PAGES` in the tests returns nothing — no test that two fonts sharing a basename, or a theory long name deriving `/source/index.html`, is refused. (b) The export's `--source-links`/`--no-source-links` mutual refusal and the before-any-network ordering (fix 8): grep for `contradict`/`no_source_links` in both test files returns nothing. (c) `_validate_map_body`'s missing-field branch, which is what guards the identity seals, is untested — only the partition and index-range branches are. (d) `--repo-root` is never exercised (the fixture takes the default).

**8. LOW — the attribute and `url()` regexes are the only eyes the rewriter *and* the gate have, and their completeness is not asserted.**
`_REF_ATTR` (`:653`) requires double-quoted `href=`/`src=`; `_CSS_URL` (`:654`) requires single-quoted `url('…')`. Anything else is silently invisible to both the rewrite and the check, so the gate cannot catch what the rewriter cannot see. §17.4 asserts two structural facts per page "because they are the whole correctness argument"; this is a third of the same weight. Measured today: zero single-quoted `href` in the rendered tree; one `src=''` (inside displayed source, correctly ignored — the scan only looks inside tag spans); all 335 rendered stylesheets use `url('…')`. **Fix:** per file, assert that the number of `href=`/`src=` occurrences inside tags equals `_REF_ATTR`'s match count, and `content.count("url(")` equals `_CSS_URL`'s.

**9. LOW — `tree_fingerprint` has no consumer.**
`:506-512, :622`. It is computed, sealed and required by `_MAP_FIELDS`, but no step ever reads or compares it — publish checks per-file sizes against `inventory` directly. Same for `theories_sha256` and `registry_fingerprint`: sealed, never compared downstream. Either give them a check (e.g. publish recomputing the fingerprint from the sealed inventory is free) or say in the docstring that they are audit values only.

**10. LOW/pedantic — injected marks nest inside whatever element is open at the line start.**
`inject_line_marks:828` prefixes the piece unconditionally; `<a id="Ln"></a>` inside an open `<a>` would be invalid nesting. Measured zero across a 300-page / 15,674-mark sample, so an unasserted invariant rather than a defect — same class as #8.

**11. LOW/elegance — two counting duplications in publish.**
`run_publish:1026-1038` keeps a `css_counters` variable overwritten once per rendered copy and used only after the loop; since the loop already asserts all copies rewrite to one text, count the externals of that one text and both `per_copy` and `css_counters` disappear. `:1050-1052` re-implements `rewrite_html_refs`'s external counting inline — the comment says "the same counting", the code is a second copy of it; a shared `_external_refs_in(content)` helper would make the claim true.

**12. LOW — comment drift.** `run_gate:1220-1221` says "A non-empty fragment against a non-markup target is a failure, not a traceback"; under D54 that holds only for composed fragments, as `test_a_fragment_into_a_binary_target_reports_instead_of_crashing` itself asserts (it expects `run_gate == 0`).

**13. LOW/pedantic — the two tree roots are inferred by string statistics rather than declared.**
`invert_theories:421-437`. ## Write Operations
- **Global throughput**: Unlimited (observed: 10M+ writes/s @ 32GB/s)

- **Batch size**: "512 MB" maximum for upsert requests
- **Embedded attributes batch**: "30 rows" per upsert batch
- **Patch by filter**: "50k" rows maximum
- **Delete by filter**: "5M" rows maximum

- **Global queries**: Unlimited (observed: 25k+ queries/s)
- **Per-namespace queries**: "5k+ queries/s"
- **Multi-query requests**: "16" queries maximum
- **Concurrent queries per unpinned namespace**: "16 (100s of queries/s)"
- **Result limit**: "10k" maximum for limit.total parameter

## Data Constraints
- **Unindexed data**: "2 GB" maximum ingested
- **Document size**: "64 MiB" maximum
- **Attribute value size**: "8 MiB" maximum
- **Filterable value size**: "4 KiB" maximum

## Schema Limits
- **Vector columns**: "8" maximum per namespace
- **Embedded attributes**: "4" maximum per namespace
- **Attribute names**: "1,024" maximum per namespace
- **Computed attributes per query**: "256" maximum

**Note**: The documentation lacks explicit details on 429 backpressure conditions, Retry-After headers, retry guidance, and "In" filter value limits.

content.content:
# turbopuffer Write Operations: Key Semantics

## patch_rows Behavior

`patch_rows` updates only specified attributes without overwriting entire documents. Critically, "Vector attributes currently cannot be patched. You currently need to retrieve and upsert the entire document." Patches targeting non-existent IDs are silently ignored—they don't create new documents.

## Adding Attributes to Existing Namespaces

New attributes can be introduced to a namespace without schema conflicts. When a document lacks a value for a newly added column, passing `null` is handled gracefully. The system simply stores `null` for those missing values across existing documents.

## Redeclaring Existing Attribute Schemas

Schema mismatches trigger errors. The documentation explicitly states: "Changing the attribute type of an existing attribute is currently an error." However, you can modify indexing behavior (like toggling `filterable` or `full_text_search`) for existing attributes without type conflicts.

## Write Backpressure & 429 Responses

turbopuffer enforces HTTP 429 backpressure when unindexed data exceeds "2 GB or 1 million rows, whichever comes first." This prevents strongly consistent queries from returning errors during heavy indexing. The `disable_backpressure` flag allows bypassing this for bulk loads, though it forces eventual consistency mode during the threshold breach.

## Recommended Retry Strategy

The documentation emphasizes batch operations for optimal throughput but doesn't specify explicit retry guidance. Standard exponential backoff with jitter is prudent when encountering 429 responses, resuming writes once indexing catches up.

content.text:
Cross-examination complete. B's arithmetic and doc claims hold up; the main thing I'd change is the ranking, because most of the tree-side findings turn out not to block the patch at all.

## Verdicts on B1–B17

**B1 (retry budget) — CONFIRM the facts, DOWNGRADE HIGH → MEDIUM-op.**
Arithmetic verified: `site_export.py:525` `attempts=6`, `delay = min(2**attempt, 60)` gives 2+4+8+16+32 = **62 s** over 5 retries. Backpressure claim verified against the docs: turbopuffer returns 429 when unindexed data exceeds "2 GB **or 1 million rows, whichever comes first**", and the per-namespace write ceiling is 10k writes/s. The run writes 1,337,009 rows at 4 workers × 4,096 rows per request, so it will cross the 1M-unindexed line and is likely to be *rate-limited by design*, not by accident. Two facts pull the severity down: a 429 that outlasts the budget raises `ExportError`, and the checkpoint has only advanced past fully-confirmed groups, so the resume is exact and `patch_rows` is idempotent per id — nothing is lost or double-written. At the documented ceiling the whole run is ~2–5 minutes, so an abort-and-resume is cheap. It is a babysitting cost, not a correctness risk.
**Converged fix:** raise the budget on the patch path only (`attempts=12` → 422 s) **and** honour a `Retry-After` header when present, plus jitter. **Cut** B's "halve in-flight": accumulation is a function of sustained write rate, not in-flight count, and halving `BATCH_WORKERS` is a guess. **Do not** reach for the documented `disable_backpressure` flag without a ruling — it forces eventual consistency during the breach, which would make the post-patch gate's namespace sample read stale rows and fail spuriously.

**B2 (dry run unmet) — CONFIRM the process gap; DOWNGRADE the `include_attributes` sub-risk to LOW; ADD a shaping requirement.**
The additive-schema shape is documented safe ("new attributes can be introduced without schema conflicts"; only *type* changes error). `include_attributes:["source_link"]` on a column-lacking namespace cannot damage anything: it is read-only, and `_gate_namespace_sample:1324` already does `row.get("source_link") or ""`, so worst case is a pre-patch gate run that 400s and tells you immediately — and post-patch the column exists, which is the only run that matters. `id In` with 500 values is genuinely undocumented and worth exercising.
**My addition, which changes the shape of B's amendment:** `run_patch:1368` refuses when `before != len(links)`, and that guard fires *before* `--limit` is consulted. So a 2k-row scratch namespace can only be patched with `--allow-count-mismatch`, which disables the very guard under test and (with B3) makes the after/before proof vacuous — the dry run would exercise a different path from production. Build the scratch namespace from a **trimmed artefact** instead: copy the artefact body, cut `records` to the ~2k sampled ids, `write_artefact` it. `_validate_map_body` still passes (the partition is over `files`, not `records`), `len(links)` then equals the scratch row count, and the production path runs verbatim — count guard, checkpoint, after/before proof and all.

**B3 (`_count()` → None) — CONFIRM MEDIUM.** `_count` returns `got.get("aggregations", {}).get("rows")`; with `--allow-count-mismatch` both `before` and `after` are `None`, `after != before` is False, and the run logs "still holds None row(s)". Note the gate is *not* affected (`count != len(links)` fails on None). Fix: raise on a non-`int` in `_count()`. One line, patch path.

**B4 (blind tail) — CONFIRM, arithmetic reproduced exactly.** n = 1,337,009: sample 500 → step 2,674, last pick index 1,334,326, **blind tail 2,682**; sample 1,000 → 1,345; sample 10,000 → **7,141** — bigger sample, bigger blind spot, exactly as B says. B's one-liner gives blind tail **0** and `len(set(...)) == sample` at 500/1,000/10,000. Adopt it, with the guard B16 implies folded in: reject `--sample < 2` rather than let `--sample 0` pass vacuously (today `chosen == []` and `len(rows) < 0` is False, so the row comparison silently disappears while the run still prints "namespace sample").

**B5 (schema literal duplicated) — CONFIRM, and it is slightly worse than B states.** The docs say a *type* change on an existing attribute is an error, but toggling `filterable`/`full_text_search` is *accepted*. So a future divergence between `namespace_schema` (`site_export.py:199`) and the patch's literal (`site_source_pages.py:1400`) either aborts a production write (type) or **silently re-indexes the live namespace** (filterable) — the silent branch is the nastier one. Fix: `schema = {"source_link": namespace_schema(0)["source_link"]}`, or expose a `SOURCE_LINK_FIELD` constant both read.

**B6 (docstring vs code) — CONFIRM; pick the doc fix.** `run_publish:955-966` does one bulk size check over `relocation` before anything is read or written; the docstring at :938 claims per-read verification. The bulk pre-loop is *better* (it fails before a single byte enters staging), so change the sentence, not the code.

**B7 (base rule) — CONFIRM, and I measured B's proposed rule on all 12 real conflicts.** B's split is right: 9 conflicts have both titles naming the symbolic path (alphabetical decides, `HOL/` beats `Unsorted/` — the good outcome), 3 are title-decided, and 2 of those 3 are my finding #2. Adding "prefer a copy whose rendered *session directory* is not an umbrella build (`AFP-*`)" as the primary key: **10 of 12 pick exactly what they pick today, and the 2 wrong ones flip** — `~~/src/HOL/Library/Tools/{smt_word,word_lib}.ML` move from `Unsorted/AFP-ALL-3/…` to `HOL/HOL-Library/…`, and their cross-references become `Word.html`, which derives `HOL-Library.Word` (verified in the artefact's `theory_pages`). `util.ML` is unaffected because **all 819 `$AFP` auxiliary copies sit under `AFP-*` sessions** (measured; zero exceptions), so the new primary key is a no-op for AFP files and degrades cleanly to the existing rule. This is the converged rule.

**B8 (title/h1 exemption severity) — converge at MEDIUM-HIGH, and note it does not block the patch.** B is right that it is harmless today; I am right that the hole is total when it fires. My probe stands: two copies whose `<pre class="source">` content is completely different merge silently when the title shares the line. What settles the severity is that the guarding invariant ("the renderer keeps `<title>` on line 6 and `<h1>` on line 12, alone") is undocumented, unasserted, and *untestable by the current test*, which is built on single-line fixtures. Silent + unbounded + unguarded = MEDIUM-HIGH, not LOW. But see the re-ranking below: it is a published-tree defect, not a patch-path one.

**B9 (D54 buckets) — CONFIRM, and I now recommend DEFERRING P1 in favour of a cheaper shape.** B's cost question is the right one and the honest answer is: there is no cheaper *computation*. Publish reads every kept page once, but references to page X are discovered after X was read, so answering them needs a second pass — i.e. a gate-equivalent walk. Worse, computing the miss set on the *published* tree (where it would be nearly free) is circular: it would assume the fragment-preservation property that P1 exists to verify. Computing it on the *rendered* tree at map time is sound but costs a full 5 GB read+regex pass that map does not currently pay.
**Converged cheaper shape, which also answers B12 and my P2:** don't compute the input's miss set — **seal it**. Freeze the 106 (target, fragment) pairs the gate already found into a small reviewed file and have the gate fail on any inherited miss *not* in that file. That delivers most of P1's safety for near-zero engineering, and it is the same mechanism the alarm baselines want. B's structural-deadness point on the strip-id hazard is accepted.

**B10 — CONFIRM, one fix.** `run_gate:1256` counts `sum(1 for r in wanted.values() if any(r))`, i.e. inherited-bearing pages only. My independent count: 9,810 pages carry our own marks, which reconciles with B's 9,870 / 9,979 / 109-invisible. Fix: report `len(pages actually read)` from the pass-2 loop.

**B11 — ACCEPT B's refinement over my #9.** Drop `tree_fingerprint` (derived from `inventory`, no consumer, zero discriminating power). **Keep** `theories_sha256` and `registry_fingerprint`: their inputs are *not* in the body, so they are the only record of which table and which registry produced the mapping — that is exactly what a seal is for. Optionally have the gate echo them so a human sees them.

**B12 — CONFIRM, merged with B9 above.** `:1248` hard-codes "baseline 106, all offset_…" in a log string, which is the weakest possible form of a baseline. Mechanism recommendation below.

**B13, B14, B15, B16, B17 — CONFIRM as stated.** B14 (`run_patch` writes its first checkpoint only after the first group lands, `:1413`) I promote to the patch-path set because it is a one-liner and its failure mode is "wrote 16k rows, then discovered the checkpoint path is unwritable". B15 I had reached independently: a reference to a dropped-but-inventoried file is always a hard error; today zero — I verified the only `session_graph` strings in the published tree are LaTeX inside displayed source, not hrefs.

**One item of mine B did not cover, and it matters for the post-patch gate:** the D54 alarm counts **distinct (page, fragment) pairs**, not references. Measured: the 106 reported pairs are pointed at by **425 reference occurrences**, one of them (`HOL.HOL.html#offset_20940..20947`) by 253. Since the post-patch gate is where the tree is re-verified, this is the number a human will read; it is 4× off from user-visible breakage and insensitive by construction (one new dead anchor referenced 5,000 times moves it by 1).

---

## The re-ranking that matters

**The merge findings do not block the patch.** An auxiliary page's published path is `aux_page(sym)` — a pure function of the symbolic position — and base selection happens at *publish* time, not map time. So changing the base rule or the tolerance leaves `file_page_map`, every composed `source_link`, and the artefact hash byte-identical; the published tree is re-generated, the links are not. My #1/#2, B7 and B8 therefore ride **after** the patch, and can even ride after the tree ships, as a re-publish.

### FINAL must-fix-before-patch (all on the patch/gate path, all small)

1. **`_count()` must raise on a non-int** (B3) — otherwise the patch's own "no row was created" proof is vacuous under `--allow-count-mismatch`.
2. **Sample every stratum including the last** (B4) — `chosen = [ids[i*(n-1)//(sample-1)] for i in range(sample)]`, plus reject `--sample < 2`. The blind tail is precisely where a truncated patch shows, and the post-patch gate is the only end-to-end evidence there will be.
3. **Derive the patch's `source_link` schema from `namespace_schema`** (B5) — a type divergence aborts the production write, a `filterable` divergence silently re-indexes it.
4. **Write a `done: 0` checkpoint before the first batch** (B14).
5. **Raise the patch's retry budget and honour `Retry-After`** (B1) — `attempts=12`, jitter; no concurrency change, no `disable_backpressure`.
6. **Run the scratch-namespace exercise** (B2), shaped with a **trimmed artefact** rather than `--allow-count-mismatch`, so the count guard, the checkpoint and the after/before proof are exercised as they will run in production. Sequence: patch → gate with `--namespace` → re-patch (must be a no-op) → re-gate.

### Rides after the patch

The whole tree side: the title/h1 tolerance (#1/B8), the base rule (#2/B7), the D54 bucket questions (#4/#5/#6, B9), the alarm-counter unit (my new finding), the gate's page-count figure (B10), `tree_fingerprint` (B11), the regex-completeness assertions (my #8), and the publish-path cosmetics B13/B15/B16/B17 and B6's docstring.

### One converged shape for #1 + #2 + B7 + B8

These three are one design, not three patches:
- **Tolerance:** normalise instead of exempt — `re.sub(r'(<(title|h1)\b[^>]*>)[^<]*', r'\1', line)` on both sides, then compare `_TAG.sub("", …)`. This makes the code literally say what the amended ruling says and closes the hole regardless of renderer line layout.
- **Merged output:** with the title text normalised away from the comparison, **rewrite the merged page's `<title>`/`<h1>` to the symbolic path**, so the page's identity no longer depends on which copy won.
- **Base:** with the title no longer at stake, choose by ownership — primary "session directory is not an umbrella `AFP-*` build", then title-names-sym, then sorted location. Measured: 10/12 unchanged, the 2 wrong ones fixed.
- **Test:** replace the single-line merge fixtures with multi-line ones whose body differs, so the test can tell the two readings apart.

---

## Position on B's patch amendments 1–5 and the post-checks

Reading amendments 1–5 as the fixes in B1–B5: **adopt 1–5**, with two changes — cut the "halve in-flight" from B1 and add `Retry-After`; reshape B2's scratch exercise around a trimmed artefact instead of `--allow-count-mismatch`. To the post-checks I would **add** one: after the patch, re-run the gate with `--namespace` **twice**, the second time after the namespace has had time to index, so a 429-era eventual-consistency read cannot be mistaken for a link mismatch. Nothing to cut.

---

## User decisions

1. **P1 (seal the input's own miss list) — my joint recommendation with B: DEFER the computation, ADOPT the sealed list now.** Instead of recomputing the rendered tree's fragment→id resolution at map time (a full 5 GB pass, and circular if done on the published tree), freeze the 106 pairs the gate already found and make the gate fail on any inherited miss outside that set. Same safety, near-zero cost, and it subsumes the alarm-baseline question.
2. **Alarm-baseline mechanism — where and how.** My recommendation: a small git-tracked file beside the plan (`expected-counters.json`) carrying D50's 232, D51's 1 with its one path, and D54's 106 pairs enumerated, passed to the gate with `--expected`. It is *reviewed* data, not derived data, so it wants to be in git where adopting a new baseline is a diff in a commit — exactly the review step the "read three numbers" discipline is asking a human for. Alternative shapes (inside the artefact; only in the plan prose) both lose that property.
3. **D49 ruling 6, amendment #2 — the base rule.** The ruling currently decides the base by title and, without saying so, thereby decides the page's cross-reference targets and the rewrite's directory context. Needs a ruling either way: adopt the ownership-first rule above (and, with it, rewriting the merged title/h1 to the symbolic path — a user-visible copy change on 12 pages, so it needs approval in its own right), or explicitly accept that a distribution ML page may link into an AFP session's clone of a theory.
4. **D54's alarm unit.** The plan and the log say "106 fragment references"; the code counts 106 distinct pairs behind 425 references. Decide which number is the standing alarm, and correct the other.
5. **Whether the tree re-publishes before or after it ships.** Since the merge fixes leave every `source_link` byte-identical, the tree can ship now and be re-published later without touching the namespace — but that means shipping the two pages with the `Zip_Benchmarks.Word` links knowingly.
